findings.message: `SCHEMA_VERSION = 1` is the only config schema that has ever existed. The only trace of an older version is `parse`'s refusal message, which `tests/test_config.py` probes with `schema_version: 0`, and nothing defines a version-0 document shape. Section 20 says only "read one older supported schema" and "produce the current schema deterministically". It never names the source version, its keys, or the key-by-key mapping to version 1. That leaves the implementer to choose between two bad options. (a) Invent a version-0 schema and its mapping, which is a speculative feature under the anti-bloat law, and 'without changing host intent' can't be judged against an invented source. (b) Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` to 2 and define a new schema, which changes the section 15 host schema and every current-version assertion in `tests/test_config.py`, well beyond this row's scope. Criterion 1, 'deterministic migration of the sole supported older schema', therefore has no fixed target, and two correct implementations could produce different bytes.
